title: One Toss and Forty Roads
subtitle: 钱币与货币 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 钱币与货币（社会服务与人际沟通·货币与消费）
meta: 主题语境：钱币与货币（社会服务与人际沟通·货币与消费）　|　核心词汇：coin　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 coin 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my grandfather ① tossed a coin to decide which of two roads the family would take, and he said the tossing was the whole of the decision. The ② coin, meaning the metal and not the paper, landed on its edge in the dust and stayed there; coin, he said, is the only thing in a pocket that is judged by which way it falls.

Every ③ coin in that house had the same weight, and the ④ coin at the end, meaning the one he kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted twice. Coin, my grandmother said, is nine parts metal and one part somebody willing to wait; my grandfather said the waiting is the part that wears out.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ coining a word was the whole of the evening, meaning the word he made and not the money. The ⑥ coin, meaning the word and not any of that, is the only thing in an evening that everybody repeats and nobody owns; coin, he said, is either something you spend or the only word that means both a metal and a word. She said the word is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ coin had become a number in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the edge. The ⑧ coin of the whole thing, my father wrote in March, was one toss and forty years of roads; coin, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand still. He said the standing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ coin I remember is the one at the end, which was minted in 1979 and is still described as the heaviest in the county. A ⑩ coin, my grandmother said in 1981, is the only thing that improves by being spent; every coin, she said, is a decision that has agreed to look like a metal. She said the decision was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 硬币（指那一枚金属硬币本身，与那些纸币相对）
C. 固定搭配：toss a coin 抛硬币（作决定）
D. n. 硬币（指那栋房子里每一枚）
E. n. 硬币（指末尾那一枚）
F. v. 创造、新造（词或短语）
G. n. 那个新造的词（抽象：他造出来的那个词本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The coin, meaning the metal and not the paper
coining a word was the whole of the evening
the coin had become a number in a ledger
The coin of the whole thing
A coin, my grandmother said in 1981

answers.why: toss a coin 意为“抛硬币（作决定）”，1961 年祖父抛硬币决定全家走哪条路。
coin 意为“硬币”，指那一枚金属硬币本身而不是那些纸币，它立在尘土里没有倒下。
coin 指那栋房子里每一枚硬币，每一枚都有同样的重量。
coin 指末尾那一枚（他留下的那一枚），是唯一有人数过两次的。
coin 作动词，意为“创造、新造（词）”，父亲说造一个词就是那个傍晚的全部。
coin 为抽象用法，指他造出来的那个词本身，是傍晚里人人重复、却无人拥有的东西。
coin 意为“硬币”，到 1974 年这枚硬币成了账本里的一个数字。
coin 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，父亲三月写道，整件事权衡下来是一次抛掷和四十年的路。
coin 意为“硬币”，我记得的是末尾那一枚，1979 年铸造，至今仍被说成全县最重的。
coin 为抽象总称，祖母说一枚硬币是唯一会因为被花掉而变好的东西。
